# Phase 0 capacity calibration

Machine: macOS arm64, 10 cores, 16 GB. Native tools: Yosys 0.70 (Homebrew), Verilator 5.052.
Peak RSS from `scripts/memrun` (`/usr/bin/time -l`, maximum resident set size). Yosys flow:
`read_verilog -sv; synth -top <top> -flatten; stat`.

## Yosys synthesis: output-stationary MAC array (generated by `scripts/gen_pe_array.py`)

| Array | Cells (after synth) | Wall time | Peak RSS |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4×4   | 14,350   | 0.9 s   | 0.10 GB |
| 8×8   | 57,357   | 3.8 s   | 0.36 GB |
| 16×16 | 229,508  | 18.0 s  | 1.32 GB |
| 32×32 | 917,766  | 88.1 s  | 4.98 GB |

Peak RSS grows about 3.7–4× per doubling of the array, i.e. about linearly in cell count
(about 5.4 KB per cell at 32×32).

**Cap for flat native synthesis: about 0.9 M cells (≈ 5 GB peak).** A flat design larger than this
exceeds the comfortable budget on the 16 GB machine (macOS and other tools also need memory). Keep
blocks hierarchical and synthesize per block above this size.

## Verilator (`scripts/verilator_calib.sh N`, `--cc --build -j 4 -O3`, 20,000 cycles)

| Array | Build wall | Build peak RSS | Run wall |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4×4   | 1.3 s | 0.23 GB | 0.35 s |
| 8×8   | 1.3 s | 0.23 GB | 0.35 s |
| 16×16 | 1.5 s | 0.23 GB | 0.33 s |
| 32×32 | 1.6 s | 0.23 GB | 0.50 s |

Not a constraint at this scale. The peak RSS is flat across sizes, so it may reflect only the largest
single process of the build; re-check with a larger design in Phase 1+.

## ORFS P&R in the VM (Nangate45, 4 ns clock, 45% utilization, `scripts/orfs_calib.sh N`)

Wrapper `pe_pr_N` (array + 32-bit XOR fold) keeps the pin count small. RSS is from `/usr/bin/time -v`
inside the VM (largest process).

| Array | Design area | Flow wall (synth to final) | Peak RSS |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8×8   | 70,849 µm²  | 3 m 09 s  | 2.4 GB |
| 16×16 | 273,427 µm² | 13 m 41 s | 5.9 GB |
| 32×32 | not run | extrapolated ≳ 55 min | extrapolated ≳ 14 GB (exceeds the 12 GB cap) |

**P&R block cap: about 230 k synthesized cells (16×16 MAC array, ~0.27 mm² in Nangate45) at about 6 GB.**
32×32 is out of budget. Plan P&R blocks of at most 16×16 PE-equivalent size (e.g. a 16×16 MXU tile, a
vector lane group, a router); full 64×64 MXUs are synthesized hierarchically and not placed.
